designObjective: Prove Reverse: 1999 as an asset-led, full-viewport editorial system: a layered moving archive stage, an asymmetric news index, and a theatrical character triptych, while keeping copper and paper colors inside their observed semantic roles and proving reuse on a source-independent held-out surface.
visualPriorityOrder: source-authentic asset identity and independent layer hierarchy

sections.firstImpressionGoal: A full-viewport moving scene dominates immediately, while the archival perimeter label and lower-right action cluster remain separate, readable layers rather than being flattened into a poster.
mustPreserve: SourceHanSerifCN only in the observed stage role
mayChange: action destinations in the fictional proof
mustNotDo: use a source screenshot as runtime
flatten the stage into one raster
replace the authored hierarchy with generic warm archive styling
promote observed typography to a global family
hide controls behind decorative media

sections.firstImpressionGoal: One strong editorial image and one denser five-row index form unequal but balanced masses, with the current category visibly distinct from available categories.
mustPreserve: selected copper versus available paper roles
mustNotDo: convert to an equal card grid
remove category state
use copper as a global primary or surface
invent hover, pressed or loading semantics
collapse the index into an undifferentiated list

sections.firstImpressionGoal: A staggered portrait selector, an oversized theatrical subject, and a narrative/voice column read as three synchronized but unequal masses.
mustNotDo: turn the surface into an avatar grid
make three equal cards
drop the selection rail
reduce the subject to decoration
claim the separate source gallery slide is equivalent

sections.firstImpressionGoal: A fictional archive briefing feels native through reused layer hierarchy, asymmetric editorial density, narrow copper-paper roles, and reversible selection without copying any source page composition one-for-one.
mustNotDo: copy a source page verbatim
reuse source screenshots
present fictional content as official
apply copper everywhere
derive an unsupported global theme

mustPreserve: identity not duplicated into equal cards

proofSurfacePlan.desktopCanvas: Independent 1280x720 source/demo captures for Home, News, Character and held-out states.
proofSurfacePlan.mobileCanvas: Independent 390x844 captures proving art-directed crop or vertical reflow without horizontal overflow.
proofSurfacePlan.inspectorPolicy: Exclude browser chrome, debug overlays, selection outlines and annotations from verdict captures.
proofSurfacePlan.sourceComparison: Compare each mapped surface at the same viewport and state; use bounded layer regions in addition to whole-canvas captures. Evaluate the held-out page only for frozen-rule reuse and explicitly fictional content.

orchestratorDecision.sourceBoundary: The observed CHARACTER state is #banner2 only; the separate #banner4 GALLERY is not treated as equivalent.
orchestratorDecision.colorBoundary: Copper and paper values remain text/border roles and may not become global fills or semantic statuses.
orchestratorDecision.publication: Keep re1999-v2 private to the migration workspace until implementation self-test, fresh independent Blind QA, fidelity gate and release checks pass.
